chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, with something similar to this, except that he mentioned that he had bequeathed to Abu Ja'far al-Mansur, and 'Abdullah, and Musa, and Muhammad ibn Ja'far, and a mawla of Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام. He said:
So Abu Ja'far said, “There is no way to kill these.”

key_terms.أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ الْمَنْصُورِ: Abu Ja'far al-Mansur, the Abbasid caliph mentioned in the report
key_terms.أَوْصَى: he made a bequest or designated in a will
key_terms.سَبِيلٌ: a way, means, or course of action
key_terms.مَوْلًى: a client, dependent, or freedman affiliated with a person
key_terms.هَؤُلَاءِ: these persons being referred to collectively

ai.seo_question: Why did Abu Ja'far say there was no way to kill those named in the bequest?
ai.summary: This report relates a statement by Abu Ja'far in response to a bequest naming several individuals. He concludes that there is no way to proceed with killing them, reflecting a political and historical circumstance tied to the succession of Imam Musa عليه السلام.
